pr_body:
If we try to merge responses with an empty response, we might take the RAW
format from an empty response over a format from a non-empty response.

Closes #84622
pr_comment: The current version takes advantage of the logic from InternalAggregations reduce which is meant to move mapped fields to the top in merges. It does this by making empty Maxes claim to be unmapped, when they might be actually empty maxes on mapped fields, so I'm a little hesitant to take care of it this way.

> The current version takes advantage of the logic from InternalAggregations reduce which is meant to move mapped fields to the top in merges. It does this by making empty Maxes claim to be unmapped, when they might be actually empty maxes on mapped fields, so I'm a little hesitant to take care of it this way.

That `isUnmapped` method is really only used for this so far as I can tell. @not-napoleon what would you think of renaming it?

I see other aggregations performing pretty similar routines. It also looks common to build "empty" aggregations for uncollected ordinals. My guess is we'd be better off renaming `isUnmapped` to `isEmpty` or `canLeadReduction`.

`isMapped` definitely seems like the wrong name.  Nothing I see in this code suggests that it cares at all about if the field it aggregated was mapped or runtime or a script or what.  As Nik says, the older convention used 'unmapped' and 'empty' somewhat interchangeably, for reasons likely lost to the mists of time.

What to rename it to is a little tricky.  `isNotEmpty` or `hasValues` seems natural, but I don't know that it's accurate.  The base method looks like it always returns true, and not every aggregation has an aggregator implementation that overrides it, so surely we must sometimes have aggregations that do not have values which return true for this method.

Given that, I think I like `canLeadReduction` for a method name.  I'm open to other ideas though.  Some javadoc about what is required to lead reduction would be good too (maybe that exists somewhere and I just didn't see it when glancing at the code).
This is failing on a cross version check on the REST API test that's expected. I'm not sure how to disable that specifically here.
Hi @tmgordeeva, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: Maybe javadoc? It's not important but may as well be consistent.
If one field isn't mapped I think we use the mapped field as the "lead" for the merge. Does this happen in production?

Bit of an off the cuff read, so I could be wrong, but I'm pretty sure we don't do that.  We've had problems around this with terms over IP fields that were unmapped in some indices, where the unmapped ones came back as keywords (the default).  Often we use `value_type` to nudge it, but I don't think anything in the merge picks the right one naturally.
It's quite possible for two aggs to have a different type and for that to have an empty type. But the "real" one will be first. Sorry for the confusion.
